newsitem.title: SWEDEN: AssiDoman says negotiating further acquisitions.
newsitem.headline: AssiDoman says negotiating further acquisitions.

text.p: Swedish forestry group AssiDoman said on Tuesday it is negotiating about further purchases, mainly in eastern and southern Europe.
"Negotiations about some further acquisitions are under way," chief executive Lennart Ahlgren told a news conference.
The company has also started discussions in Asia, but nothing will happen there for about a year, Ahlgren said.
AssiDoman has set aside 5 billion-8 billion crowns for investments this year. Of the total, four billion crowns will be used at existing plants, Ahlgren said.
Ahlgren stressed that the investment level will fall significantly next year and in 1999.
"The level of investments will be much lower in 1998 and 1999," he said.
"Then we will concentrate on operating the company as efficiently as possible," he said, adding that there would be no large investments in existing plants during those two years.
AssiDoman posted a 56 percent fall in first quarter profit after financial items to 360 million crowns on Tuesday.
